response.sql:
WITH order_executions AS (
  SELECT 
    o.recordvault,
    o.timespan,
    AVG(oe.fillcount) FILTER (WHERE oe.fillcount IS NOT NULL) AS avg_fill
  FROM orders o
  INNER JOIN orderexecutions oe ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.recordvault, o.timespan
),
timespan_means AS (
  SELECT 
    timespan,
    AVG(avg_fill) AS mean_avg_fill
  FROM order_executions
  WHERE avg_fill IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY timespan
),
filtered_orders AS (
  SELECT 
    oe.recordvault,
    oe.timespan,
    oe.avg_fill,
    (oe.avg_fill - tm.mean_avg_fill) AS exceeds,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY oe.timespan ORDER BY oe.avg_fill DESC) AS rank_in_timespan
  FROM order_executions oe
  JOIN timespan_means tm ON oe.timespan = tm.timespan
  WHERE oe.avg_fill IS NOT NULL
    AND oe.avg_fill > tm.mean_avg_fill
)
SELECT 
  recordvault AS ordersmark,
  timespan,
  avg_fill,
  exceeds,
  rank_in_timespan
FROM filtered_orders
WHERE rank_in_timespan <= 3
ORDER BY timespan, rank_in_timespan;

assumptions.assumption: NULL fillcount values are excluded from per-order averages (not treated as zero). An execution with NULL fillcount contributes nothing to its order's average.
Orders without any executions are implicitly excluded, as 'drop unmatched executions' and the average-per-order logic presumes each order has at least one execution to average over.

alternatives.interpretation: NULL fillcount values should be treated as zero in the per-order average, rather than excluded entirely.

  SELECT 
    o.recordvault,
    o.timespan,

  FROM orders o
  INNER JOIN orderexecutions oe ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.recordvault, o.timespan
),
timespan_means AS (
  SELECT 
    timespan,
    AVG(avg_fill) AS mean_avg_fill
  FROM order_executions
  GROUP BY timespan
),
filtered_orders AS (
  SELECT 
    oe.recordvault,
    oe.timespan,
    oe.avg_fill,
    (oe.avg_fill - tm.mean_avg_fill) AS exceeds,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY oe.timespan ORDER BY oe.avg_fill DESC) AS rank_in_timespan
  FROM order_executions oe
  JOIN timespan_means tm ON oe.timespan = tm.timespan
  WHERE oe.avg_fill > tm.mean_avg_fill
)
SELECT 
  recordvault AS ordersmark,
  timespan,
  avg_fill,
  exceeds,
  rank_in_timespan
FROM filtered_orders
WHERE rank_in_timespan <= 3
